Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNPreBuild

The gate before code. Nothing gets built until every source has been checked and every gap has
been named.

**Intended model: Opus 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — set it
yourself before invoking. The plan synthesis step delegates to the `zm-planner` agent, which is
pinned to Opus regardless of the session model, so the expensive judgement runs on Opus either
way.

**Input:** `- let's work https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-742` — a Jira key (e.g. `SFCC-194`), optionally followed by a depth.
If no key is given, ask for one before doing anything else.

## Depth

Depth is a parameter, not an adverb. Pick one and say which you are using:

| Depth | Jira + Confluence | Codebase | Figma |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quick` | the ticket and its direct links | branch state, file tiers | the named node only |
| `standard` *(default)* | ticket, links, comments; targeted Confluence search | tiers, blast radius, nearest existing pattern | node, variants, states |
| `exhaustive` | full link graph, all comments, related epics, all matching Confluence | above, plus every consumer of every touched file and the exemplar PR diffs | node, all variants, all states, all viewports, token mapping |

Never substitute a stronger adverb for a depth. "In-depth full-on exhaustive" is not a level;
`exhaustive` is.

---

## Phase 0 — position

Call `/session-start`. It confirms the branch, reads the tracking docs, runs health checks and
states current position.

Then confirm one thing it does not: **you cannot be on `develop` or `main`.** A `PreToolUse` hook
blocks every Write and Edit on those branches, so a plan handed to the builder from `develop` is
dead on arrival. If the branch is wrong, say so and stop — do not create a branch unasked.

---

## Phase 1 — gather

Run these **in parallel**. Each one ends in its own findings block. Never let a clean source hide
a broken one — report all five, even when four are fine.

### Jira — `mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue`

Pull the story and read all of it: description, requirements, acceptance criteria, linked design,
attachments, linked work items, and the full comment thread. Comments routinely carry the
decision that contradicts the description.

Flag: missing or untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments ·
no linked design · attachments referenced in prose but not attached · linked work items that are
still open and block this one · a decision made in comments that never made it into the description.

### Confluence — `confluence_search`, `confluence_get_page`

Search for anything bearing on this story: TSDs, integration docs, data dictionaries, decisions.

Flag: no TSD where the work clearly needs one · a TSD that contradicts the ticket · documentation
describing an approach the codebase does not implement · a page last updated before a decision
that supersedes it.

### FED handbook — `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md`

The build approach: tokens, components, CSS structure, overriding, accessibility, tests, stories.
Part I is the machine, Part II the procedure, Part III the role.

Flag: handbook guidance that contradicts what the codebase now does · a claim whose cited
`file:line` no longer resolves · anything the story needs that the handbook does not cover.

The handbook is a derived account, not the source. **Where it disagrees with
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, that file wins** — and say so, because it means the handbook
is stale.

### Codebase

Branch state, and the shape of what is about to be touched.

- Confirm `develop` is current with `origin/develop`.
- For every likely-touched file: tier and owner, from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and
  `protectedFiles.md`. **Never from `.claude/registry/*.md`** — its Tier column is a derived
  heuristic and is wrong in places.
- Call `/audit-tier <path>` for anything you are unsure about. It also returns import blast radius.
- Find the nearest existing pattern. This codebase has strong precedent; matching it is cheaper
  and more reviewable than inventing.
- Read the exemplar PRs when the story touches their surface: **PR #64** (ui-kit atom/molecule,
  four-file pattern, co-located recipe, render-slot wiring), **PR #59** (global-chrome component,
  co-located recipe with shared cross-file values), **PR #56** (pure token layer, no component
  change).

Flag: any Tier 1 file in the likely set · high blast radius (a shared file with many consumers) ·
work that crosses squad territory · an existing pattern the story would contradict.

### Figma

- Design System 2026 — `https://www.figma.com/design/wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/Zimmermann_Design_System_2026`
- Zimmermann_Designs — `https://www.figma.com/design/QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs/Zimmermann_Designs`

**Ask for one node URL per variant and per state**, not one per component. If the file-level
links are not enough to resolve the specific component, stop and ask Marcel. Do not guess at
which node the story means, and do not build from a neighbouring node that looks close.

Check:

- **Completeness** — every variant and every state: hover, focus, active, disabled, loading,
  error, empty, success.
- **Currency** — is this design archived or superseded? Triage archived against current before
  anyone builds to it. An archived node that still renders is a trap.
- **Tokenisation** — does every value map to an existing `--zimm-*` token, or is a new token
  being introduced? A new token is Tier 1 and needs the designer.
- **Responsiveness** — frames exist at 402 / 1023 / 1440; breakpoint tokens are 768 / 860 / 1024.
  **The 768–1022 band is unframed**, so anything in it is an inference, not a design.

Two measurement traps that have produced false defects here. Flag a comparison that hits either:

- **Node type decides comparability.** Figma TEXT nodes report a cap-height box, which is not
  comparable to a CSS line box — never file a mismatch from one. FRAMES and INSTANCES report a
  real box and are directly comparable.
- **The two Figma files must never be cross-compared.** The Design System file and the Designs
  file are different sources; a delta between them is not a defect.

**No design is a blocker, not licence to invent.** If the ACs name something Figma does not have,
that is a finding for Marcel — or an explicit **provisional**, labelled as such and carried into
the plan as an assumption. Never fill the gap silently.

Flag: missing variants or states · a design that is archived or superseded · values with no token
· the unframed tablet band left to inference · a design that contradicts an established component
· no design at all where the story implies one.

---

## Phase 2 — reuse

These already exist. Call them; do not reimplement them.

1. `/feature-spec` — turns the gathered picture into a scoped implementation plan and emits a
   ready-to-paste scoped prompt.
2. `/scope-check` — run it **on that prompt**. It verdicts SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED and rewrites
   risky prompts. This is the highest-leverage gate available; do not skip it.
3. `/audit-tier <path>` — per file, wherever scope-check flags something specific.

Two known traps when calling these:

- `/code-quality` defaults to diffing against **`main`**; `/pr-checklist` diffs against
  **`develop`**. On a feature branch these give different file sets. Always pass explicit scope.
- `/pr-checklist` already calls `/code-quality` internally. Calling both doubles the audit.

None of these skills emits machine-readable output — they all return prose for a human. If you
need to branch on a result, restate the verdict yourself rather than parsing theirs.

---

## Phase 3 — the gate

This is the part that earns the skill. Produce one table, every source, every gap:

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Severity is one of:

- 🔴 **BLOCKED** — cannot plan around it. A missing AC, an absent design, a Tier 1 file with no
  owner approval, a `scope-check` BLOCKED verdict. **Stop here.** Report and wait for Marcel.
- 🟡 **CLARIFY** — plannable, but the plan carries a stated assumption. Name the assumption
  explicitly in the plan so it is visible if it turns out wrong.
- 🔵 **NOTE** — worth knowing, does not affect the plan.

**Do not fill a gap with an assumption and carry on silently.** A missing acceptance criterion is
a finding, not something to infer. The whole point of the gate is that it stops.

---

## Phase 4 — plan

Delegate to the `zm-planner` agent (Opus). Give it everything gathered — all five findings blocks,
the `/feature-spec` output, and the `/scope-check` verdict.

It returns: goal statement · scale call (multi-commit or multi-branch, with reasoning) · file
manifest with tiers and owners · steps with concrete pass criteria · per-step loop configuration ·
open questions.

Write the result to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`, and write the Phase 3 gate
table to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/findings.md`.

Create the run directory if it does not exist. **Never write run state into the repo.**

---

## Phase 5 — handoff

Present to Marcel, in **"ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead"** register — not dumbed down, but without
jargon that gets in the way. Lead with the consequence, then the mechanism, then the fix.

1. The gate table — blockers first.
2. The plan summary — scale call, step count, file count with tier breakdown.
3. Every stated assumption, gathered in one place.
4. The paths to `plan.md` and `findings.md`.

Then say plainly whether this is ready for `zimmerMANNBuild`, or what is blocking it.

**Put decisions to him one at a time, using AskUserQuestion.** Do not present a wall of choices
and do not bundle unrelated calls into one question.

**This skill stops here. It never invokes `zimmerMANNBuild`** — Marcel does, once he has read the
gate. Discover → report → wait for approval → and execution is a separate, deliberate act.

**Do not hand off with an unresolved 🔴.** Handing a blocked plan to the builder is how a
build burns an afternoon on the wrong thing.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never modify anything.** This skill reads, checks and plans. The only files it writes are
  under `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/`. No repo file is touched — not one.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `zimmermann-pwa/.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
  `CODEOWNERS`, `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. All Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never infer squad ownership** from `squadA.md` / `squadB.md`. They contradict each other on
  PDP/PLP and are both drafts. Read `CODEOWNERS`.
- **Never present a gap as resolved because it seems minor.** Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Say what you did not check.** A source you skipped is itself a finding.
- **Provenance, not proximity.** A document living in the codebase is a downstream artifact, not
  a source. If you cannot locate the original source for a claim, flag it **provenance unknown**
  and ask. Never fabricate a source, and never fall back to citing a codebase path as one.
- **Local-only docs are never citable.** `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` and its predecessors are
  Marcel's personal files. **They must never appear in a PR, a commit message, or a code
  comment.** Where the same rule exists in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`, cite the repo file
  instead — that is the citable source.
- **Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full treatment. At `quick` depth,
  drop the exemplar-PR read and the blast-radius sweep, and keep the gate. Nothing too crazy,
  no overthinking.

This agent should be invoked after a TypeScript Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. - code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

(Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- plugin-dev:agent-creator: Use this agent when the user asks to "create an agent", "generate an agent", "build a new agent", "make me an agent that...", or describes agent functionality they need. Trigger when user wants to create autonomous agents for plugins. Examples:

<example>
Context: User wants to create a code review agent
user: "Create an agent that reviews code for quality issues"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate the agent configuration."
<commentary>
User requesting new agent creation, trigger agent-creator to generate it.
</commentary>
</example>

</commentary>

user: "Add an agent to my plugin that validates configurations"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate a configuration validator agent."

Plugin development with agent addition, trigger agent-creator.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Write, Read)

- plugin-dev:plugin-validator: Use this agent when the user asks to "validate my plugin", "check plugin structure", "verify plugin is correct", "validate plugin.json", "check plugin files", or mentions plugin validation. Also trigger proactively after user creates or modifies plugin components. Examples:

<example>

user: "I've created my first plugin with commands and hooks"

</commentary>

- plugin-dev:skill-reviewer: Use this agent when the user has created or modified a skill and needs quality review, asks to "review my skill", "check skill quality", "improve skill description", or wants to ensure skill follows best practices. Trigger proactively after skill creation. Examples:

user: "I've created a PDF processing skill"

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)

- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

## ac642cf1-e1c8-4490-9caa-814476453870
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

Run the mandatory session start ritual defined in [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). Do this before writing any code.

## Steps (in order — do not skip any)

1. **Confirm branch** — run `git branch --show-current`. If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — no edits permitted (see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 1). If it matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`, read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) in full before proceeding — the supervised-edit and back-merge rules there apply on top of the Hard Rules.

2. **Read tracking docs** — read these in parallel:
   - [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md) — current phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending
   - [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](../../../.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) — what exists this sprint, what is deferred. **Read before scoping any new work.**
   - [.docs/memory/feedback.md](../../../.docs/memory/feedback.md) — patterns to avoid or repeat
   - [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md) — current `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version and review state
   - [../session-notes.md](../session-notes.md) — lightweight, **gitignored, per-developer** carryover notes from your last local session (a Claude-writable staging area — see "Living Memory" below for how this differs from `.docs/memory/`). If it has pending items, surface them in step 4's "blockers or outstanding issues" and clear/promote each once resolved. It won't exist for a fresh clone or a teammate who hasn't used it — that's expected, skip silently.

3. **Health checks** — run when the helper exists:
   - `bash scripts/healthCheckAll.sh` — If the script does not exist yet, state that clearly and skip.

4. **State current position** — in plain language, say exactly:
   - Current branch
   - Current sprint / phase (from `projectState.md`)
   - The last completed task and the next task
   - Any blockers or outstanding issues

   Format: "Resuming from: [last completed task]. Next: [next task]. [Any blockers or health issues]."

5. **Confirm readiness** — ask if the user wants to proceed with the stated next task or redirect to something else.

Do not write any code until this ritual is complete and the user has confirmed direction.

---

## Living Memory — what belongs where

`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Keep it current — update the relevant file whenever a session produces new information that belongs there.

**`.claude/session-notes.md` is different: a lightweight, Claude-writable, gitignored, per-developer staging area** (same pattern as `userProfile.md` below, but for tasks rather than profile info) for short-lived carryover items (e.g. "still need to do X next session") that haven't been promoted to `.docs/memory/` yet. It's **not** shared via git — each developer's notes stay local, so they never conflict or overwrite a teammate's. Unlike the files below, Claude may write to it directly. Use it for quick pending-item tracking; move anything durable and team-relevant into the right `.docs/memory/` file once it's confirmed, and clear the note.

| File | What belongs there | When to update |
|---|---|---|
| `architecture.md` | Stack decisions, overrides pattern, key paths, structural choices | A new integration is added, a structural decision is made, or a key path changes |
| `projectState.md` | Phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending, unresolved dependencies | Any integration goes live, a phase changes, a feature is completed, or a dependency is resolved |
| `feedback.md` | What worked, what failed, patterns to avoid or repeat | After discovering a gotcha, a failed approach, or a validated pattern |
| `references.md` | Service URLs, API keys, credentials, logins, dashboards | A new credential or service URL is introduced (system roles live in `architecture.md`) |
| `userProfile.md` | User's role, expertise, working style, preferences | User shares a preference or working-style detail that should persist |

**Rules:**
- Never leave a file with only its placeholder comment — populate it the moment you learn something that belongs there.
- **No duplication.** Every fact has exactly one home. Before writing something, check whether it already lives in another doc — if it does, reference that doc instead of copying. Applies across all `.md` files: `AGENTS.md`, memory files, and PRDs.
- **Conciseness.** Keep all `.md` instructions concise.
Jira's in. Now let me fan out — tracking docs, health checks, the Jira link graph, and codebase state, all in parallel.

content.content:
############ Part I §5 Figma to code ############
### 5. Figma to code

#### The discriminator is node type, not a fudge factor

- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`,
  `text-box-edge: cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Measured artifacts:
  "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs 18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — a delta here is a
  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against 45/68 was a real gap, and a naive
  "it's just cap height" rule would have wrongly dismissed it.

**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one
is a defect. Three contact items all sitting at +7 after every real cause was removed = the
heading's cap box.

**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.css.ts`, deriving from
`lineHeight` + 4.5px padding produced 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

#### There are two Figma files and comparisons must be like-for-like

`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (design system) and `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states).
Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page
file produced two wrong conclusions in a row — first "the slot is 59px in both states"
(actually `Subscribed=False` 320×44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap
change 40→24: the design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix
that suppressed intended growth when the 68px padded box was already correct.

#### Frames are not breakpoints

Frames exist at 402/1023/1440; breakpoint tokens are 768/860/1024. The unframed **768–1022
band was genuinely broken** — 18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels — and covers three iPad
models in portrait. `flexWrap: nowrap` prevents *breaking*, not *shrinking*: the row refused to
break, so the words broke instead.

#### Type metrics

The fallback stack renders roughly **13% wider** than Futura Round, which is why serving the
real faces matters for parity review. `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable
families and is useless — compare widths instead.

#### Measurement method

**Subtract non-component bands before comparing totals** — the footer compares against 476,
not 606, once the `Disclaimer` band is excluded. **Isolate causes by cumulative in-DOM
mutation, one candidate at a time.** Measure `y` relative to the component root (Figma reports
frame-relative coordinates). Use

fixes at mobile** — two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only because a taller sibling column masked
them.

it, and don't silently ignore it. Document the deviation at the point of use.

beside Figma found it.

### 6. Layout mechanics

############ Play 1 — reuse & dependency check ############
### Play 1 — The reuse & dependency check

Four rungs: use as-is → override → compose existing atoms → build new. Rung 4 is rarest and
needs justification.

**Where to look:** `.claude/registry/` for `Origin` (`Custom` / `Override` / **`Base`**), then
`ui-kits/`. ⚠️ The registry's `Tier` column is unreliable — `generateRegistry.mjs:133-215`
hardcodes tiers, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything to Tier 4.

**`Origin = Base` is the hidden cost.** It means copy-first: mirror the file, convert to TS,
verify the override renders, *then* build. That's real effort and it belongs in the estimate.
Eight components referenced throughout `.claude/rules/` are still base.

**The `shared/ui` barrel exception.** Overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` to propagate styling into
base cart/checkout/account looks like enormous leverage. It intercepts nothing — the barrel
re-exports relatively, which the resolver doesn't rewrite, and 212 base files import the barrel
(195 excluding tests) while **0** import the individual module. Don't scope a story around it.

**Duplicate atoms are a human problem.** No tool detects "this is a second Button." The fix
that makes it self-service is one line in the BA's story template: *name the component, and
state whether it exists.*

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/
```

Tier by composition (what the component's own template renders), camelCase for
Zimmermann-authored, a registered recipe always.

⚠️ **The rules set is split on this.** `components.md` and `conventions.md` contain **zero**
occurrences of `ui-kits`, `atoms`, `molecules` or `organisms`. `new-component/SKILL.md:29`
still scaffolds to the flat path. `.docs/architecture.md` contradicts itself. Reconciling this
is a standing item.

# SFCC-742 — Wishlist – Login Panel Content · PreBuild gate

**Depth:** `standard`
**Run date:** 2026-09-01
**Verdict:** 🔴 **BLOCKED — 3 blockers. No plan written. Do not hand to `zimmerMANNBuild`.**

| | |
|---|---|
| Story | [SFCC-742](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-742) — Story, 3 pts, High |
| Status | Ready for Development (reached 2026-09-01 15:40) |
| Epic | SFCC-2 PWA Kit Components |
| Sprint | SFCC Sprint 4 |
| Assignee | Jersey Perez Jr |
| Reporter | Jasmijn Tsang |
| Session branch | `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-ui-colour-swatches-variation-selection` (wrong branch for this story) |
| `develop` currency | current with `origin/develop` @ `f7fd816`; working tree clean |

---

## Gate table

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Jira | **The acceptance criteria contradict the story's own scope statement.** The description says the component "covers the panel content only — the drawer shell, slide-in behaviour, overlay, and close trigger are owned by `pdp/drawer` (SFCC-736)… renders as children passed into that shell." But **ACs 1, 2, 9, 10 and 11 all assert shell behaviour**: slides in from the right, close icon dismisses it, focus moves in and is trapped, focus returns to the trigger, `role=dialog` + `aria-label`. A component passed in as `children` owns none of those. This decides the public API (does it take `isOpen`/`onClose`, or nothing at all?), where the file lives, and which ACs are even testable. | 🔴 BLOCKED | Jasmijn/Hazel confirm one reading. See "Decision 1" below — both options are concrete. |
| 2 | Jira + GitHub | **The hard dependency is unmerged and currently un-mergeable.** `ZimmDrawer` / `ZimmPdpDrawer` exist only on `feature/sfcc-736-pdp-drawer-tabs` — PR [#67](https://github.com/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pull/67), `reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED`, **`mergeable: CONFLICTING`**, last pushed 2026-08-31. Hazel's own comment on SFCC-742 (2026-08-25): *"Will be picked up once drawer component is completed."* Severity is conditional on #1: under the content-only reading the panel needs nothing from #67 to be **built**, only to be **placed**; under the self-contained reading it cannot start. | 🔴 BLOCKED | Either #67 merges, or #1 resolves to content-only so this can proceed in parallel. |
| 3 | Jira | **The two interactive controls this story needs are separately scoped, unstarted stories in the same squad's backlog.** AC 5 (Apple + Google) is [SFCC-590](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-590) *Login – Social Sign-In Buttons (Apple & Google)* (Squad-A, To Do, CRM-001) and overlaps [SFCC-347](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-347) *Checkout – Social Sign-In Buttons*. AC 4 (email + Send Code for OTP) is [SFCC-588](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-588) *Login – OTP Verification Input (Email)*. Building them inside SFCC-742 creates the duplicate-atom problem the FED handbook (Play 1) flags as **undetectable by any tool**. | 🔴 BLOCKED | Decide which story owns each control, and sequence accordingly. |
| 4 | Codebase | **`ZimmButton` has no leading-icon slot.** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx` renders `{label}` alone for `primary`/`secondary`; the `icon` variant is an `IconButton` with no visible text. The design needs " SIGN IN WITH APPLE" and "G SIGN IN WITH GOOGLE" — icon **and** label. Extending it touches a shared `ui-kits/atoms/` component (3 real component consumers today: `zimmInputAction`, `zimmSubscribeModal`, `zimmNavItem`; PR #67 adds `zimmDrawer`). This is the largest unestimated piece of work in a 3-point story, and it is the same work as #3. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Falls out of #3. If SFCC-742 owns it, the `ZimmButton` extension must be in the plan and the estimate revisited. |
| 5 | Codebase + Figma | **`ZimmTextInput` is the wrong Textfield variant.** `zimmTextInput.css.ts:96` renders `borderBottom` only, and its own header comment says it implements *"Figma Textfield flush variant (node 40000265:374)"*. The wishlist design uses a **full 1px box border** on all four sides (verified at 1400px against node `40001889:38498`). Adding a boxed variant is another shared-atom change. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Confirm a boxed Textfield variant is in scope, or that the flush variant is an accepted deviation. |
| 6 | Codebase | **`ZimmInputAction` is the tempting reuse and it is wrong here.** It renders an input with a *trailing icon-button* inside the field. The design stacks the Email field and a full-width SEND CODE button as **separate** elements. Compose `ZimmTextInput` + `ZimmButton` directly instead. | 🔵 NOTE | Recorded so the builder doesn't reach for it. |
| 7 | Figma | **The panel has exactly one state.** Only `Variant=Default` exists for `Tab=Wishlist`. Sibling tabs in the same component set carry `Step 01/02/03`, `Filled`, `Selected`, `Success`. So there is **no design for AC 8** (content fails to load), none for the email error state, and none for a pending/loading SEND CODE — despite that being an async call in the real flow. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Either Kiera supplies the states, or the plan carries explicit stated assumptions (inherit `zimmTextInput`'s existing `errorText` treatment; AC 8 = render nothing rather than a broken frame). |
| 8 | Figma | **The heading is not in this component.** The design models the panel as `Tab=Wishlist` inside the `pdp/drawer/content` component set. The content begins at *"You must log in or create an account to add items to your wishlist."* — the "WISHLIST" title lives in `pdp/drawer/header`. **AC 3 ("displays a heading and explanatory copy") is only half-satisfiable here.** | 🟡 CLARIFY | Folds into Decision 1. |
| 9 | Figma | **The Jira link points at a whole canvas, not the component.** `node-id=40000938-5082` is the `└– Drawer 🟢` page — 774K of XML, 3116 frames. The real nodes are `40001889:38489` (Large 522×523), `40001889:38498` (Small 342×559), `40001897:40903` (Mobile 342×503). Resolved here, but the ticket should carry one URL per variant. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Update `Design/Technical Notes` on the ticket with the three node URLs. |
| 10 | Jira | **Squad ownership contradicts itself.** `labels` still say `Squad-A`; the `Squad` custom field was changed **Squad A → Squad B** by Hazel on 2026-08-25. CODEOWNERS routes `ui-kits/**` to *both* squads, so the merge isn't blocked — but who reviews and who is accountable is currently undefined. | 🟡 CLARIFY | One of the two fields is wrong. |
| 11 | Jira | **DoR was self-certified five seconds before the transition.** Automation bounced the story back to Tech design twice on 2026-09-01 (12:09, 15:30) for an incomplete checklist. At 15:39:55 Hazel added `Technical approach understood, Design available, Dependencies identified, Testable`; at 15:40:00 she transitioned it to Ready for Development. *Dependencies identified* is true. *Dependencies resolved* is not — see #2. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Worth naming at standup rather than treating the status as a green light. |
| 12 | Codebase + Figma | **Divider colour token drift.** Figma's `alias/color/border/secondary` = `#dddddd`. The repo's `border.secondary` → `grey[200]` = **`#d1d1d1`** (`theme/foundation/colour.ts:13,73`). Same alias name, different value; both files claim the 2026 Design System as their source, so **provenance is unresolved from here**. `theme/foundation/` is **Tier 1**. | 🟡 CLARIFY | UI designer call. Not a build fix — do not "correct" either side silently. |
| 13 | Codebase | **The known button-height conflict is live for this story.** Figma `alias/size/action/height/1300` = 52, matching `actionSizes.height.lg` = `'52px'`. But `zimmButton.css.ts:205` `BTN_HEIGHT_LG = '50px'` — the already-flagged, still-unresolved provisional. All four CTAs in this panel render 2px short of the design. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Pre-existing and already logged in `overrideStyling.md`; flagged because this story is the one that surfaces it visually. |
| 14 | Confluence | **No TSD, and the microcopy has no source but the Figma frame.** SFCC-742 carries no requirement ID — labels are just `Custom` + `Squad-A`, unlike its siblings (SFCC-588/589/590 carry `CRM-001`, SFCC-347 carries `CFD-001/011`). So *"You must log in or create an account to add items to your wishlist."* and *"Join for exclusive offers, early access and a more personal experience."* trace to **no requirement, no PRD row and no TSD** — only the design. | 🟡 CLARIFY | **Provenance unknown.** Confirm the copy is final, and whether it goes through `useUiCopy`/Contentful (translatable) or ships as literals. |
| 15 | Jira | **A componentisation request was deleted rather than answered.** The original description (pre-2026-08-21) read: *"@Kiera — this component is not yet componentized in the Design System Figma. The design exists in the PDP drawers section (node 40001369-36097). Please extract into a named component before dev picks this up."* Jasmijn's rewrite removed it. It **appears** actioned — the `Tab=Wishlist` symbols now exist — but node `40001369:36097` is not on the linked canvas, and nobody recorded the handover. | 🔵 NOTE | Confirm with Kiera rather than assume. |
| 16 | Jira | **AC 12 targets WCAG 2.1 AA; `AGENTS.md` targets 2.2 AA**, with 2.1 as a documented fallback only where 2.2 is infeasible. | 🔵 NOTE | Build to 2.2 AA; the AC is a floor, not a ceiling. |
| 17 | Jira | Malformed prop table in the description (`\|Prop\| \|Values\|Notes\|` — header/row cell counts don't match). Cosmetic. | 🔵 NOTE | — |
| 18 | Jira | **Naming drifts from the sibling story.** The design calls it `pdp/drawer/content` `Tab=Wishlist`; sibling [SFCC-847](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-847) is titled `drawer/content/filters`; this one is "Wishlist – Login Panel Content". Three conventions for one component family. | 🔵 NOTE | — |
| 19 | Codebase | **No Tier 1 or Tier 2 file is in the likely set.** Target `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**` → `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` (CODEOWNERS:176); co-located `*.css.ts` → same (CODEOWNERS:186). Tier 3, squad review only. Tier read from `CODEOWNERS` + `frozenFiles.md` + `protectedFiles.md` directly, **not** from `.claude/registry/` (its Tier column is a derived heuristic). The only Tier 1 exposure is #12, which is a designer decision, not a build step. | 🔵 NOTE | Authenticated `gh` login `marcelannavarro` **is** in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` — so even the `colour.ts` route is open procedurally. Still a designer call. |
| 20 | Figma | **Every value tokenises.** All colour, space and type variables on the node map to existing `--zimm-*` families — `#191919`→`grey[900]`, `#666666`→`grey[600]`, `#707070`→`grey[500]`, spacing 4/16/24/32/40 → `2xs`/`m`/`xl`/`2xl`/`3xl`. **No new token needs authoring**, so no Tier 1 foundation change is required for the build itself. Sole exception is the `#dddddd` drift (#12). | 🔵 NOTE | Good news — recorded so it isn't re-litigated. |
| 21 | Figma | **Tablet band is inference, as always.** Wishlist frames exist at 522 (Large) and 342 (Small *and* Mobile). Small and Mobile share a width and differ only in height (559 vs 503) — the distinction is vertical rhythm, not width. Breakpoints remain 768/860/1024, so 768–1022 is unframed. | 🔵 NOTE | — |

---

## Decision 1 — the one that unblocks the rest

Both readings are internally coherent. They produce **different components**.

**Option A — content-only (matches the description).**
`ZimmWishlistLoginPanel` takes no `isOpen`/`onClose`. The caller (SFCC-434) wraps it:
`<ZimmDrawer isOpen … onClose … size="large" aria-label="Wishlist"><ZimmWishlistLoginPanel size="large" /></ZimmDrawer>`.
ACs 1, 2, 9, 10, 11 move to SFCC-736/SFCC-434 — they are already satisfied by `ZimmDrawer`, which gets focus trap, focus restore, Escape and overlay-click free from Chakra's `Drawer`. AC 3's heading moves to the drawer header. **This story can start before PR #67 merges** — it has no compile-time dependency on it.

**Option B — self-contained drawer organism (matches the ACs).**
`ZimmWishlistLoginPanel` takes `isOpen`/`onClose`/`size` and composes `ZimmDrawer` internally. All 12 ACs are testable in one place. **Hard-blocked on PR #67**, which is currently `CONFLICTING`.

Option A is the better engineering call — it matches the description, matches how the design is modelled (`Tab=Wishlist` content inside `pdp/drawer/content`), matches the precedent PR #67 already set with `detailsAndCareContent.tsx`, and it decouples the story from a conflicted branch. But **it is not mine to decide**, because it silently drops five ACs onto another story.

---

## What was NOT checked

Stated explicitly, per the skill's own rule.

- **Phase 2 was not run.** `/feature-spec` and `/scope-check` were skipped — the gate stopped first, and a scoped prompt built on an unresolved API contradiction would be worse than none.
- **Confluence was one targeted search**, not a full tree walk. `04.72 Component Design & User Story Tracker` (408944644) and `1.5 Web Design (UX)` (268075023) were surfaced but **not opened** — either could carry a per-component sign-off status for this panel.
- **The `Zimmermann_Designs` file (`QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs`) was not opened.** Correct per the two-file rule, but it means composed page states for this panel are unverified.
- **Contentful was not checked** for existing `uiCopy` keys covering this panel's microcopy.
- **Exemplar PRs #64 / #59 / #56 were not diffed.** The pattern was read directly from the shipped exemplars (`zimmSubscribeSection`, `zimmInputAction`, `zimmTextInput`) plus PR #67, which is the actual dependency.
- **No `/audit-tier` call was made** — the target path does not exist yet, so tier was derived from `CODEOWNERS` + the two rules files directly.

---

## Nearest existing pattern (for whenever this is unblocked)

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/` is a near-exact structural match and should be the template:

- `index.tsx` — `useMultiStyleConfig('<Recipe>')`, microcopy via `useUiCopy()` with English fallbacks, business data via props
- `<name>.css.ts` — co-located recipe, `var(--zimm-*)` only, explicit media queries off `BP` (never Chakra's array shorthand — `recipeGuards.test.ts` fails the build on bare token keys)
- `index.stories.tsx` — `Commerce/` or `Layout/` category
- `index.test.tsx` — mocks children whose internals are proven elsewhere; tests only this component's own contract
- register the recipe in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`

## 0. Two findings that change the brief

### 0.1 `ZimmButton` cannot render a labelled button with a glyph — the social buttons are blocked on an atom gap

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx` is a discriminated union:

- `ZimmLabelButtonProps` (`variant: 'primary' | 'secondary'`) — **has no icon prop at all**.
- `ZimmIconButtonProps` (`variant: 'icon'`) — icon-**only**, renders a Chakra `IconButton` with
  `aria-label` and no visible text.

Figma requires `SIGN IN WITH APPLE` / `SIGN IN WITH GOOGLE` as **outlined button + leading glyph +
label**. That shape does not exist today. Compounding it, `ZimmIcon`'s `ZimmIconType` union is closed
at 34 entries against Figma iconography node `1892:59595` and contains **no apple/google** — so the
existing `icon` variant could not render them even if the union allowed a label.

**Decision: add an optional `leadingIcon?: React.ReactNode` to `ZimmLabelButtonProps`** (Step 1).
Rationale:

- Purely **additive** to one member of a discriminated union — no existing call site changes, proven
  by `npx tsc --noEmit`.
- Typed as `ReactNode`, not `ZimmIconType`, so it **sidesteps the design-system icon-set question
  entirely**: the organism passes `<AppleIcon />` / `<GoogleIcon />` from the barrel directly, and
  the Figma-locked 34-icon `ZimmIconType` union is not touched.
- Keeps **one button entry point** for all five buttons in the panel. The alternative (three buttons
  via `ZimmButton`, two via raw Chakra `<Button leftIcon>`) is inconsistent at review.
- `variant="secondary"` is confirmed to be the outlined treatment (transparent bg,
  `var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid`, `borderColor: var(--zimm-color-text-default)`) with
  `_hover` / `_active` / `_disabled` / `_focusVisible` already defined — so the social and
  Create-an-Account buttons inherit fully-specified states with zero new style authoring.

**Documented fallback if a reviewer objects to widening a shared atom:** render only the two social
buttons inline in the organism as Chakra `<Button variant="secondary" leftIcon={...}>`. Same recipe,
same styling source of truth (`zimmButton.css.ts` stays canonical either way — `.zimm-btn-*` classes
do not exist and must not be introduced). This is a fallback, not the plan.

**Not doing:** no change to `zimmButton.css.ts`. Chakra's default `leftIcon` gap applies. No measured
Figma gap value was available and `overrideStyling.md` forbids inventing one — see Open Question 5.

### 0.2 `ZimmPdpDrawer` does **not** thread `size` down to tab content

Verified on `origin/feature/sfcc-736-pdp-drawer-tabs` @ `a05b257`:

```
ZimmPdpDrawer({ isOpen, onClose, size, tabs, initialTabId, ariaLabel })
  → renders  activeTab.content  inside a role="tabpanel"
```

`content` is a pre-built `React.ReactNode`. The shell passes `size` to `ZimmDrawer` and `ZimmTabs`
but **never to the content node**. So whoever assembles the `tabs` array (SFCC-434) must set this
component's `size` at construction time.

That creates a real desync risk: `zimmDrawer.css.ts` collapses **every** size variant to the mobile
treatment below `breakpoints.md` via media query, regardless of the `size` value passed. If the
content component drove layout off the `size` prop alone, a viewport at 500px would render a mobile
*shell* wrapping large *content*.

**Decision: keep the `size` prop (AC7 names Large/Small/Mobile explicitly, and Marcel fixed it), but
mirror `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s mechanism exactly** — each recipe variant's overrides live *inside* an
`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})` block, so below tablet all three variants collapse to the
shared `baseStyle` mobile treatment automatically, in lockstep with the shell. This satisfies AC7,
honours the fixed decision, obeys the explicit-media-query rule, and cannot desync from the shell.
Surfaced as Open Question 6.

---

## 2. Override vs custom — **custom, and there is no copy-first step**

Assessed explicitly, per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule.

- The target path is `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistLoginPanel/`.
  `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` has **no `ui-kits/` directory at all**
  (verified). There is **no mirrored base file**, therefore no copy-first obligation.
- Base SFCC *does* ship adjacent components — `login/`, `standard-login/`, `passwordless-login/`,
  `social-login/`, `otp-auth/`, `social-icons/`. **None is the right thing to override for this
  story**, for three independent reasons:
  1. `social-login/index.jsx` calls `useAuthHelper(AuthHelpers.AuthorizeIDP)` and reads
     `getConfig()?.app?.login?.social?.redirectURI` — **auth logic, explicitly out of scope**.
  2. `passwordless-login/index.jsx` requires a react-hook-form `form` instance and owns a
     `showPasswordView` state machine — a content-only component must not own that.
  3. Both import `Button` from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui` — the
     **`shared/ui` barrel trap**: overriding a member of that barrel intercepts nothing, so they
     would not pick up Zimmermann button styling even if overridden.
- Those base components are the integration seam for the **future auth story** (SFCC-434 / CRM), not
  this one. Recorded so a later planner does not re-litigate it.

**Conclusion: 100% net-new Zimmermann components. No file is copied from `node_modules`. No
`console.log` override-proof step. Steps 1–4 below contain no copy-first phase, deliberately.**

Styling approach is likewise settled by the rules, not invented: `textStyle` for type,
`var(--zimm-*)` for colour/spacing, one namespaced `ZimmWishlistLoginPanel` recipe co-located as
`zimmWishlistLoginPanel.css.ts`, registered in `theme/components/index.ts`. `breakpoints` is imported
from `app/theme/foundation` — **not** `footerShared.ts`'s `BP`, which its own header scopes
footer-only; `zimmDrawer.css.ts` sets the precedent of importing `breakpoints` directly, and matching
it keeps this component in lockstep with the shell it renders inside.

---

## 7. Stated assumptions

Carry these into the PR description verbatim.

1. **Both Apple and Google buttons are built**, per Figma and AC5 — despite `.docs/prd/account.md`
   CRM-001 marking SSO "not yet in scope" and Confluence 04.2 recording a marketing objection to
   Apple login. Marcel's explicit decision; the BA is raising the PRD conflict separately. One of
   `checkout.md` / `account.md` needs correcting either way.
2. **`Variant=Default` only.** No OTP six-box code-entry screen: no Figma node exists for it, and
   auth logic is out of scope. `SEND CODE` is wired to a caller-supplied callback and has no
   designed next state in this story.
3. **ACs 1, 2, 9, 10, 11 are satisfied by SFCC-736's shell and are not reimplemented here.** Chakra's
   `Drawer` supplies focus trap, initial focus, focus restore, scroll lock and Escape/overlay close;
   `DrawerContent` supplies `role="dialog"`; `ZimmDrawer` owns the close button. They are asserted at
   the assembly level once PR #67 merges — **explicitly deferred, not dropped**.
4. **`size` is a locally-declared union**, structurally identical to `ZimmDrawerSize`, swapped to the
   shared import in a follow-up once #67 merges. No import from an unmerged branch.
5. **Copy is read via `useUiCopy()` with English fallbacks** matching Figma verbatim. This story
   authors **no** Contentful entries and touches **no** file under `translations/` (Tier 2).
6. **Social-button glyph gap is inherited** from the Chakra Button default. No measured Figma value
   was available; `overrideStyling.md` forbids inventing one.
7. **No heading element is rendered by this component** — AC3's "heading" is read as the drawer
   shell's tab title. Pending Open Question 2.
8. **Base-template `AppleIcon`/`GoogleIcon` are used as-is**, under the icon barrel's own banner
   "not in the Zimmermann Figma spec but available for use". Visual parity unverified.
9. **The Small Figma variant (`40001889:38498`) was never rendered visually** — enumerated only.
   Large and Mobile were confirmed structurally identical, so risk is low but real.

**Blocking the handoff** (answer before or during Step 3):

1. **AC3 heading — does this component render one?** The designed panel (all sizes) opens with
   explanatory copy only; the heading appears to be the shell's tab title. The plan assumes **no
   heading**. If the answer is "yes", Step 3's markup and Step 4's assertions both change.
   *Owner: Jasmijn Tsang (reporter) / Kiera (design).*

**Not blocking the build, but blocking sign-off or a follow-up:**

2. **Copy source ownership.** Which `wishlist.loginPanel.*` Contentful `uiCopy` keys, authored by
   whom — and given 8 storefronts plus Transperfect, is `translations/` (Tier 2) the right home
   instead? **This does not block the build**: `t(key, fallback)` returns the fallback with no
   Provider and for unknown keys, so the component renders identical output whether or not the
   entries exist. Using `useUiCopy` from the start is strictly dominant and fully reversible.
   *Owner: Integration / SI partner.*
3. **Apple/Google glyph parity.** Do the base-template marks match the Figma glyphs? If not, request
   the assets from the designer — do not substitute a visually different icon (AGENTS.md > Rules >
   Icons). *Owner: Kiera / design.*
4. **`ZimmDrawer` + title, or `ZimmPdpDrawer` + a single tab?** Arguably SFCC-434's wiring decision,
   but it determines the demo story once #67 lands, and `ZimmPdpDrawer` requires a tab label whereas
   `ZimmDrawer` requires a `labelledBy`/`aria-label`. *Owner: Marcel / SFCC-434 owner.*
5. **NEW — does the social button's leading glyph recolour with the label** on hover / active /
   disabled? `Tab=Wishlist` has only `Variant=Default`, so no Figma node answers this. If yes, the
   glyph needs `currentColor` fill and the base-template icons may not honour it.
   *Owner: Kiera / design.*

   `ZimmTabs` but **not** to `activeTab.content`, so the tabs assembler (SFCC-434) must set it at
   construction. Confirm that is the intended contract, or ask SFCC-736 to thread `size` into the
   content node. The plan's media-query-inside-variant structure makes a desync visually harmless,
   but the contract is still unspecified. *Owner: SFCC-736 / SFCC-434 owners.*

**Recorded, no action needed:** ownership ambiguity (Jira `customfield_10237` says Squad B, labels say
`Squad-A`, assignee is Jersey Perez Jr) does not block review — CODEOWNERS routes `ui-kits/**` to both
squads regardless.

behaviour**.

content.content:
new interactive states (they all live one layer down in `zimmButton.css.ts` / `zimmTextInput.css.ts`,
already shipped and signed off). Over-scaled machinery would be a defect here, so:

**Running:**
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test`, `npm run audit:tokens` at **every** commit.
  These are cheap, and `npm run test` transitively runs `recipeGuards.test.ts`, which is the
  mechanical enforcement of both the bare-token ban and the `Zimm*` namespacing rule.
- **One** Vitest file (Step 4), scoped to this component's own contract.
- **One** Storybook story file with an a11y check for AC12.
- **One** consolidated CodeRabbit pass (`cr review --light --base develop`) before the PR, per
  AGENTS.md step 4 — not per commit.

**Deliberately NOT running, with reasons:**
- **No Playwright spec and no `.feature` file.** This component completes no user journey on its own
  — ACs 1/2/9/10 are drawer-shell behaviours that do not exist on `develop` until PR #67 merges.
  Additionally, per `.claude/rules/testing.md` > Change-scoped E2E, a `develop`-targeted PR touching
  paths no `@area` allow-list claims resolves to `e2e_scope: skip` and would not run a PR-time E2E
  suite anyway. E2E belongs to the assembly story (SFCC-434), not here.
- **No per-commit Tester/Scorer cycle.** One loop config per step (§6) is sufficient at this size;
  a full adversarial pass per commit is over-scaled for 3 points.
=== loop config table ===
## 6. Loop configuration

Story-specific. Generic "works correctly" is not a gate.

| Step | Tester checks | Scorer PASS |
|---|---|---|

**SFCC-742 "Wishlist – Login Panel Content"** (Sprint 4, 3 pts, epic SFCC-2, assignee Jersey Perez Jr)
was PreBuild-gated **twice on 2026-09-01** — first pass 14:25 (adjudicated with Marcel, 2 × 🔴 cleared,
plan written 14:31), second independent pass ~16:30. Artefacts:
`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-742/` — `findings.md`, `findings-addendum-2.md`, `plan.md`
(amended; `plan.md.bak-preamend` holds the pre-amendment copy).

**The recurring trap this surfaced: Zimmermann's shared `ui-kits/atoms/` do not cover the design
system's full variant surface, and the gap is invisible to every automated gate.** Two instances on
this one story:

- `ZimmButton` — `primary`/`secondary` render `{label}` only, **no icon slot**; the `icon` variant is
  icon-only. Cannot build "SIGN IN WITH APPLE" (glyph + label).
- `ZimmTextInput` — the recipe has `parts` + `baseStyle` and **no `variants` key at all**; its only
  border is `borderBottom` (flush underline). Cannot build a boxed field. No `variant` prop exists.

Both were resolved the same way (Marcel, 2026-09-01): **extend the atom, additive, defaulting to the
existing behaviour** so no current consumer changes. Expect the same gap on **SFCC-588** (Login – OTP
Verification Input), **SFCC-590** (Login – Social Sign-In Buttons) and **SFCC-347** (Checkout – Social
Sign-In Buttons) — all Squad-A, all To Do, all needing these same controls. Adding `leadingIcon` under
SFCC-742 **pre-empts SFCC-590**, which should be re-pointed to "consume the atom" rather than
re-estimated as "build the buttons."

**Why no gate catches it:** `tsc`, eslint, vitest, CodeRabbit and the Storybook a11y run all pass with
the wrong border or a missing glyph slot. Only rendering beside Figma finds it — consistent with
[[prove-dont-assert]] and the FED handbook's "no automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect."

Two token conflicts confirmed live on this panel, both pre-existing and **not this story's to fix**:
`zimmButton.css.ts` `BTN_HEIGHT_LG = 50px` vs Figma/Handover **52px** (`actionSizes.height.lg`), and
Figma `alias/color/border/secondary` **#dddddd** vs repo `grey[200]` **#d1d1d1** — same alias name,
two values, both citing the 2026 Design System, provenance unresolved. Both are UI-designer calls.
See [[project-styling-layer-boundary]] and [[project-chakra-scale-registration]].

Dependency: **PR #67** (`feature/sfcc-736-pdp-drawer-tabs`, SFCC-736 `pdp/drawer`) is
`REVIEW_REQUIRED` **and `mergeable: CONFLICTING`** as of 2026-09-01. The plan correctly builds from
`develop` and only designs the seam against #67. ACs 1/2/9/10/11 are shell-satisfied by Chakra's
`Drawer` inside `ZimmDrawer` and must not be reimplemented in the content component.
